rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract, not a tuned design. Geometry: five line sensors in a row at y = 0.03 m (ahead of the axle, so they see the line before the wheels reach it), spaced 1 cm apart from x = -0.02 to +0.02 m. The 12 mm footprint overlaps neighbours and always covers part of the 25 mm tape. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn rate. Mass 0.8 kg is mid-range. Body width 0.18 m sets the off-track limit to about 0.0575 m (tape half-width 0.0125 + 0.045), which is just inside the 0.06 m floor and gives some margin. Controller: sensor weights are antisymmetric (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1), so the signal is zero on the centre line and grows with offset, with positive signal steering left as the contract requires. kp = 3.0 gives a moderate steering response; ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves; kd = 0.2 adds light damping. base_speed = 1.6 (about 80% of full PWM) aims for the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish within 3 s, leaving headroom for slower bends. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot keeps turning toward where the line was last seen. Expected result: completion on the oval, with some oscillation on the slalom. If progress stalls or the robot leaves the track on sharp bends, I expect to reduce base_speed or raise kd. Hypotheses to check: (1) kp = 3 is not oscillatory at 1.6 speed; (2) the 5-sensor spread is enough to keep the line under the array on the s-bend; (3) completion time is under 3 s.
